transfers.source_mechanism: oscillatory contraction generates pressure differentials, enabling directional flow through network paths, which then drives structural reinforcement of high-flow channels and weakening of low-flow channels
source_conditions: variable flow rates through different paths
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: adaptive network optimization through flow-dependent structural remodeling
transfers.required_translation: replace physical contraction with signal timing adjustments, replace pressure differentials with traffic flow incentives, replace structural material with timing plan flexibility, replace thickening/thinning channels with green time allocation changes
transfers.expected_effect: traffic signals adapt their timing based on local flow conditions, creating a self-organizing network that optimizes traffic flow without central coordination
boundary_conditions: each intersection has only local traffic measurements
signal timing adjustments must be gradual to avoid instability
failure_conditions: uniform traffic flow eliminates flow differentials
communication failures prevent coordination between neighbors
transfers.testable_prediction: after an incident creates a flow imbalance, the adaptive signal network will redistribute green time to favor high-flow corridors within 15 minutes, reducing total travel time by at least 12% compared to the fixed-timing system
